publicationMetadataPlan.creator: OpenAI built-in image generation
publicationMetadataPlan.mediaDescription: No generated media; these conditional feeding, diet, iodine, and iron cautions do not resolve a single product, protocol, patient state, or non-prescriptive physical subject
publicationMetadataPlan.sourceUse: Current controlled records, clinical guidance, and local source-resolution evidence define asset-free scientific holds.

controlFinalReview.reviewer: WikiBiome Control Tower clinical safety, scientific, source-resolution, and editorial audit

reviewStandard: Clinical-caution pages may not receive generic warning graphics, crossed-out food or supplement imagery, disease anatomy used as a proxy for a treatment claim, elemental-metal media substituted for a clinical formulation, or an image that conceals a patient-specific exception. All six routes fail before prompt creation.
promotionRule: No Batch 115 source hash exists or is eligible for promotion. All six routes remain asset-free scientific holds. No generated source, master, derivative, registry record, endpoint, Schema object, social preview, or image-sitemap entry may be created from this batch.

routeDecisions.reason: The page has no linked evidence and turns a neonatal feeding decision into a categorical STOP. It does not resolve gestational age, birth weight, maternal or donor milk availability, preterm formula, human-milk fortifier, feed timing, volume, probiotic protocol, NICU setting, comparator, growth needs, or NEC outcome definition. Current guidance preserves formula as a conditional option when human milk is unavailable and recognizes fortification needs. A bottle, breast, infant bowel, formula powder, supplement, or prohibition scene would imply a feeding directive and erase those clinical contingencies.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Add direct neonatal evidence and current guideline context; define gestational age, birth weight, feeding substrate and product, donor-milk availability, fortifier, probiotic strain and dose if relevant, feed timing and volume, NICU protocol, population, comparator, growth and NEC outcomes, contraindications, and emergency exceptions; then identify a non-prescriptive physical subject.

routeDecisions.reason: The route combines high-protein low-carbohydrate and ketogenic diets even though they are distinct controlled diet concepts. It does not define macronutrient composition, protein source, energy intake, CKD stage, albuminuria, dialysis status, diabetes, weight-loss intent, duration, population, comparator, renal outcomes, or malnutrition safeguards. Current kidney guidance individualizes protein intake and notes that dialysis can increase protein needs. A kidney, meat plate, ketone, food collage, or crossed-out meal would visually collapse incompatible diets and patient states into a universal instruction.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Separate ketogenic from high-protein low-carbohydrate scope; define exact macronutrient and energy composition, protein source, CKD stage, albuminuria, dialysis status, comorbidities, nutritional status, duration, population, comparator, renal and metabolic outcomes, monitoring, and contraindications; then define a non-prescriptive representation.

routeDecisions.reason: The route does not select an iodine compound, supplement product, dose, baseline iodine status, pregnancy state, thyroid hormone state, antithyroid therapy, radioiodine context, population, comparator, monitoring, or outcome. Iodine is an essential nutrient, while excess and deficiency can have different effects and susceptibility varies in autoimmune thyroid disease. A thyroid, iodine crystal, salt, seaweed, pill, or prohibition symbol would imply a categorical clinical instruction and duplicate disease imagery without representing the actual intervention state.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define iodine compound and source, product and lot, elemental iodine content, dose and duration, baseline iodine and thyroid status, Graves phenotype, pregnancy status, concurrent therapy, population, comparator, monitoring, outcomes, adverse events, and contraindications; reconcile the title to current guidance before a new media audit.

routeDecisions.reason: The route does not resolve supplement form, product, dose, dietary iodine exposure, baseline deficiency, pregnancy, thyroid function, autoantibody state, levothyroxine therapy, population, comparator, monitoring, or outcome. Susceptibility to excess iodine can differ in autoimmune thyroid disease, but that does not make every iodine source or clinical state equivalent. A thyroid, iodized salt, seaweed, pill, or crossed-out supplement would turn a conditional risk boundary into a universal prohibition and would not be distinct from the reviewed Hashimoto disease image.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define iodine compound and source, product and lot, elemental content, dose and duration, dietary intake, baseline iodine and thyroid status, autoantibodies, pregnancy, concurrent therapy, population, comparator, monitoring, outcomes, adverse events, and contraindications; reconcile the title to current guidance before any visual prompt.

routeDecisions.reason: The route treats iron supplementation as one object even though oral and intravenous products, ferrous and ferric compounds, elemental doses, absorption, inflammatory activity, bleeding, deficiency, and anemia status differ. Current gastroenterology guidance supports iron repletion in IBD with route selected by inflammation, absorption, response, and tolerance. A bowel, iron atom, tablet, infusion, blood cell, or crossed-out supplement would imply stopping treatment and could be unsafe for an iron-deficient patient. The reviewed elemental Iron asset is not a clinical supplement and cannot be reused as a proxy.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Define Crohn or ulcerative-colitis phenotype and activity, iron deficiency and anemia criteria, oral or intravenous route, exact compound and formulation, elemental dose, schedule, duration, absorption and tolerance, bleeding state, population, comparator, monitoring, outcomes, adverse events, and escalation rules; reconcile the categorical title to current guidance.

routeDecisions.reason: The four linked records describe metal associations and mechanisms rather than a clinical trial establishing a universal iron-supplement avoidance rule in Alzheimer disease. The route does not define iron deficiency or anemia, systemic versus brain iron measures, formulation, route, elemental dose, disease stage, comorbidities, population, comparator, monitoring, cognitive or safety outcomes, or treatment context. A brain, plaque, iron atom, pill, infusion, or prohibition scene would convert associative evidence into a treatment directive; the elemental Iron and Alzheimer disease assets cannot be combined as proof of the claim.
routeDecisions.requiredResolution: Add direct clinical supplementation evidence and guidance; define deficiency, anemia and overload criteria, systemic and CNS biomarkers, exact formulation and route, elemental dose and duration, Alzheimer phenotype and stage, comorbidities, population, comparator, monitoring, cognitive and safety outcomes, and contraindications before any new media audit.
